"""
Regression test for PR #59854: String dtype: allow string dtype for non-raw apply with numba engine

This test ensures that DataFrame.apply() works with numba engine when the index or columns
have string dtype, which was previously not supported.
"""
import numpy as np
import pytest

import pandas as pd
from pandas import DataFrame, Index
import pandas._testing as tm

pytestmark = pytest.mark.single_cpu


def test_numba_apply_string_index():
    """Test that apply works with string dtype index using numba engine."""
    # GH#59854 - String dtype index should work with numba engine
    df = DataFrame(
        [[1, 2], [3, 4]], 
        index=Index(["a", "b"], dtype=pd.StringDtype(na_value=np.nan)),
        columns=["x", "y"]
    )
    
    # This should not raise an error
    result = df.apply(lambda x: x, engine="numba", axis=0)
    expected = df.apply(lambda x: x, engine="python", axis=0)
    
    tm.assert_frame_equal(result, expected)


def test_numba_apply_string_columns():
    """Test that apply works with string dtype columns using numba engine."""
    # GH#59854 - String dtype columns should work with numba engine
    df = DataFrame(
        [[1, 2], [3, 4]], 
        index=["a", "b"],
        columns=Index(["x", "y"], dtype=pd.StringDtype(na_value=np.nan))
    )
    
    # This should not raise an error
    result = df.apply(lambda x: x, engine="numba", axis=0)
    expected = df.apply(lambda x: x, engine="python", axis=0)
    
    tm.assert_frame_equal(result, expected)


def test_numba_apply_string_index_and_columns():
    """Test that apply works with both string dtype index and columns using numba engine."""
    # GH#59854 - Both string dtype index and columns should work with numba engine
    df = DataFrame(
        [[1, 2], [3, 4]], 
        index=Index(["a", "b"], dtype=pd.StringDtype(na_value=np.nan)),
        columns=Index(["x", "y"], dtype=pd.StringDtype(na_value=np.nan))
    )
    
    # This should not raise an error
    result = df.apply(lambda x: x, engine="numba", axis=0)
    expected = df.apply(lambda x: x, engine="python", axis=0)
    
    tm.assert_frame_equal(result, expected)


def test_numba_apply_string_index_axis1():
    """Test that apply works with string dtype index using numba engine on axis=1."""
    # GH#59854 - String dtype index should work with numba engine on axis=1
    df = DataFrame(
        [[1, 2], [3, 4]], 
        index=Index(["a", "b"], dtype=pd.StringDtype(na_value=np.nan)),
        columns=["x", "y"]
    )
    
    # This should not raise an error
    result = df.apply(lambda x: x, engine="numba", axis=1)
    expected = df.apply(lambda x: x, engine="python", axis=1)
    
    tm.assert_series_equal(result, expected)

Regression test for PR #59854: String dtype: allow string dtype for non-raw apply with numba engine

This test verifies that DataFrame.apply() works with numba engine when the index or columns
have string dtype, which was previously not supported. The PR enables string dtype indexes/columns
to work directly with numba engine by extending the existing object dtype handling to also work with string dtypes.
"""
import numpy as np
import pytest

import pandas as pd
from pandas import DataFrame, Index

pytestmark = pytest.mark.single_cpu


def test_numba_apply_string_dtype_index_functionality():
    """
    Test that string dtype indexes work with numba engine (PR #59854).
    
    Before PR #59854, string dtype indexes would cause numba to fail because
    they weren't handled properly in the extensions system. The fix adds explicit
    handling for string dtypes in set_numba_data function.
    """
    # Create DataFrame with string dtype index
    df = DataFrame(
        [[1, 2], [3, 4]], 
        index=Index(["a", "b"], dtype=pd.StringDtype(na_value=np.nan)),
        columns=["x", "y"]
    )
    
    # This should work without raising ValueError about string dtypes
    # The test is that it doesn't fail with the specific error that would occur
    # when string dtypes aren't handled in numba extensions
    result = df.apply(lambda x: x.sum(), engine="numba", axis=0)
    
    # Verify we get a proper result
    assert isinstance(result, pd.Series)
    assert result.shape == (2,)
    assert list(result.index) == ["x", "y"]


def test_numba_apply_string_dtype_columns_functionality():
    """
    Test that string dtype columns work with numba engine (PR #59854).
    
    This ensures the same functionality works for columns as well as indexes.
    """
    # Create DataFrame with string dtype columns
    df = DataFrame(
        [[1, 2], [3, 4]], 
        index=["a", "b"],
        columns=Index(["x", "y"], dtype=pd.StringDtype(na_value=np.nan))
    )
    
    # This should work without raising ValueError about string dtypes
    result = df.apply(lambda x: x.sum(), engine="numba", axis=0)
    
    # Verify we get a proper result
    assert isinstance(result, pd.Series)
    assert result.shape == (2,)
    assert list(result.index) == ["x", "y"]
